 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , owner and insurer of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 asserting that on 21.08.2021 at 1.30 p.m. when travelling by sitting in a passenger autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01- AK-4861 from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road,
near Greens Bar, Agara flyover upper ramp, HSR layout, driver of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , drove the same negligently, dashed the same to container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 which was negligently parked , thereby caused the accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Green View hospital, East point hospital , Bengaluru by spending Rs.3,00,000/-.

3. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 24 years, used to earn Rs.50,000/p.m. by maintaining a tailoring shop.

4. In response to the notice respondent No.1, owner of the autorickshaw , respondent No.2-insurer of the autorickshaw , respondent No.4 insurer of lorry appeared through their respective Advocates Thanisha Shaik Alias Thanusha vs Shivaram on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106852366/

sentences.text: In the written statements respondents No.1 and 2 owner and insurer of the autorickshaw asserted that due to sole negligence of the driver of the lorry , the accident taken place.
6. In the written statement respondent No.4 insurer of the lorry asserted that due to the sole negligence of the driver of the autorickshaw , the accident taken place.
7. Inspite of service of notice respondent No.3 owner of the lorry remained absent.

8. On the basis of the pleadings on 28.06.2022, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was travelling as a passenger in the Ola autorickshaw bearing reg. No.KA-01- AK-4861 and he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 21.08.2021?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order?
9. On 27.07.2022, 07.09.2022, 21.10.2022, 07.12.2022, 02.08.2023 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 18 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.18.
On 21.06.2023 , 09.08.2023 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.H.Manjunatha as PW2 and produced 3 documents at Ex.P.19 to P.21.

On 25.09.2023, 04.01.2024, 11.01.2024 respondent No.2 produced the evidence of F.D.A. in R.T.O., HSR layout, S.D.A. in R.T.O., Jayanagar, officer of the 2nd respondent/insurance company as RW1, 2 and 4 get produced 5 documents at Ex.R.1 to 4 and 6.
On 11.10.2023, 09.01.2024 respondent No.4 produced the evidence of its officer as RW3 and produced the copy of the policy at Ex.R.5.
10. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 filed notes of arguments along with copy of six judgments.
11. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of the petitioner, respondent No.2 and 4 and perused the records.

12. On the basis of material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 .... Due to the negligent use of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 and negligent use of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 at the ratio 50:50,

 REASONS  13. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner/PW1 stated that on 21.08.2021 at 1.30 p.m. when travelling by sitting in a passenger autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK- 4861 from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road, near Greens Bar, Agara flyover upper ramp, HSR layout, driver of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , drove the same negligently, dashed the same to a negligently parked container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 on the middle of the road, thereby caused the accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.
14.
In the written statements respondents No.1 and 2 owner and insurer of the autorickshaw asserted that due to the sole negligence of the parking of the lorry , the accident taken place.
15. In written statement respondent No.4 the insurer of the lorry stated that due to the sole negligent driving of the autorickshaw by its driver, accident taken place.
16. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that when travelling by sitting in an autorickshaw from K.R.Puram towards Silk Board on ring road/fly over accident taken place.
Petitioner submitted ignorance to the suggestion that the place of accident is a busy traffic area.
Petitioner admitted that the lorry was parked in the center of the road without any indication or signal.
Petitioner stated that she never observed the accident place as the lorry was parked in the middle of the road without any indication or signal.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that the accident taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
Petitioner submitted filing of complaint regarding accident after one day of the accident.

In the cross-examination made on behalf of respondent No.4,
petitioner stated that the driver of autorickshaw in which she was a passenger was driving it rashly and negligently.

17. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Manjunath , RW1 and 2 staff of R.T.O., HSR layout, staff of R.T.O. ,
Jayanagar stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

18. In the evidence affidavit RW2 and 4 officer of insurance companies, hear say witnesses Thanisha Shaik Alias Thanusha vs Shivaram on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106852366/

Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar recorded on 22.08.2021, Ex.P.4 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident,
Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report ,
20.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the Medico Legal Case Report, in which the reason for the injuries are noted as alleged accident i.e., autorickshaw has hit by lorry .

Ex.P.10 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by HSR layout traffic police in crime No.38/2021 against Ashif Ali Khan driver of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 , Yogesh, driver of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , Shivaram owner of autorickshaw for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279,283, 338 of IPC,
section 56,192 of IMV Act.
21 . In this case, evidence of the driver of the autorickshaw, driver of the lorry and independent eye witness are not available.

Hence, I have concluded that on 21.08.2021 at 1.30 p.m. when petitioner was travelling by sitting in a passenger autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK- 4861 from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road, near Greens Bar, Agara flyover upper ramp, HSR layout, due to the negligence use of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , negligent use of the container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 at the ratio 50:50 accident taken place between rear part of lorry and front part of autorickshaw resulting in the injuries.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 accordingly.
22. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered cut injury over inner aspect of lower lip with outer lip (lip laceration), fracture distal end of radius right side, severe injuries to head, hand legs , took first aid at Green View hospital, then took treatment at East Point Hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 21.08.2021 to 24.08.2021, underwent surgery by spending Rs.3,00,000/-.
23.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.50,000/p.m. by maintaining a Ladies Tailoring shop.
In the written statement respondents No.2, 1 and 4 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
24. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion that in the accident suffered only simple injuries neither taken treatment as an inpatient nor underwent surgery.
Petitioner submitted ignorance about the name of the doctor who treated her.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that bills produced at Sl.No3,4 and 9 are not concerned to her.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that bills at Sl.No.18 is not standing in her name.
Petitioner admitted that bills produced at Sl.No.5,6 and 19 are deposit receipts.
Petitioner admitted lack of docucments regarding her tailoring work.

sentences.text: Petitioner admitted that as per Ex.P.17 and P.18 income tax returns for the financial year 2020-21 and 2021-22 , the annual profit are Rs.3,23,394/- and Rs.4,20,100/- respectively.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on 07.12.2022 she is doing the same business and earning more than what was earned prior to the date of accident.
26. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Manjunath stated that on 11.03.2023 when clinically examined noticed that the petitioner suffered disability at 20% to right wrist, left knee and 10% to whole body.
In the evidence PW2 produced OP record and IP record and x-rays at Ex.P.19 to P.21.
In the cross-examination PW2 stated that he was the head in the team of doctors who have treated the petitioner and his name is mentioned in the discharge summary.

PW2 admitted that when petitioner came for clinical examination fracture injury wrist fracture and injury in the knee are united and explained that the stiffness remained at the time of assessment of disability.
27. In the evidence respondents No.1, 2 and 4 stated nothing regarding the nature and consequences of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

28. Wound certificate , discharge summary , case file, x-ray, medical bills excluding advance bills,
bills pertaining to treatment provided to dental problem shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of distal end of right radius , cut injury over inner aspect of lower lip with outer lip,
took treatment at East Point hospital as an inpatient from 21.08.2021 to 24.08.2021, then taken follow up treatment by spending Rs.44,378/-.
29.

As referred above, the points elicited during cross-examination of petitioner shows that the income of the petitioner has been increased comparing to the date of cross-examination and date of accident.
In the evidence PW2 submitted that fracture of the petitioner are united and injury suffered by the petitioner in the accident are healed.
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of the PW2 Dr.Manjunath are insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

30. Hence, I award Rs.60,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.44,378/- towards treatment charges, Rs.5,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.75,000/-
(15,000x5) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
31. Therefore, I came to the conclusion that petitioner is entitle of Rs.2,24,378/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
32. Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.4 shows that as on the date of accident container lorry bearing MH-05- AM-1759 had insurance coverage with respondent No.4.
In this case, there are no evidence to shows that as on the date of evidence, respondent No.3 owner of the lorry had contravened any terms of the policy.

Copy of the B register extract marked at Ex.R.2 shows that since 29.04.2019 to 28.04.2021 autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01- AK-4861 had Fitness Certificate to run at Bengaluru outer area and since 31.01.2020 to 30.01.2025 autorickshaw had permit to run in Bengaluru outer area (KA41, KA50, KQ51).
35. In the evidence RW1 FDA , RTO ,HSR layout stated that FC of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 was valid upto 28.04.2021, thereafter owner of the autorickshaw has not renewed the FC.
RW1 stated that as on 21.08.2021, there was no FC to autorickshaw and if FC is not renewed the vehicle cannot run on public road.
36. In the evidence RW2 , SDA , R.T.O. Jayanagar, stated that Yogish is having DL to ride two wheeler and LMV (Non-Transport) and he can drive goods vehicle upto the laden weight of 7,500 kgs.
RW1 stated that driver Yogesh had no DL to drive passenger autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 as on 21.08.2021.
RW2 stated that if driver had no licence to drive passenger autorickshaw , he cannot drive passenger autorickshaw on public road.
37. In the cross-examination , RW2 stated that as per Ex.R.4 DL is valid from 24.02.2016 to 05.01.2034.
RW2 denied the suggestion that if a person can drive goods vehicle upto the laden weight of 7500 kgs through LMV driving licence, he can drive auto also.
38. In this case evidence of Yogesh , the person who drove the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 is not produced.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on 21.08.2021 Yogesh had valid licence to drive passenger autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 .

sentences.text: Hence, the judgments cited on behalf of the respondent No.2 insurance company are directly applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
39. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 is not eligible to be indemnified by the respondent No.2 insurance company .
Hence, respondent No.1 owner of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 alone is liable to pay 50% of the total compensation awarded above to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,24,378/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a.

The respondent No.1 being the owner of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 shall pay Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6%
p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 shall deposit Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., within 3 months from today.

The respondents No.3 and 4 being the owner and insurer of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
Respondent No.4 being the insurer of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 shall deposit Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to her bank account directly.
The petition filed by the petitioner against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that the accident taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
Petitioner submitted filing of complaint regarding accident after one day of the accident.
In the evidence PW2 submitted that fracture of the petitioner are united and injury suffered by the petitioner in the accident are healed.

8. On the basis of the pleadings on 28.06.2022, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was travelling as a passenger in the Ola autorickshaw bearing reg. No.KA-01- AK-4861 and he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 21.08.2021?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of the PW2 Dr.Manjunath are insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.
In this case, there are no evidence to shows that as on the date of evidence, respondent No.3 owner of the lorry had contravened any terms of the policy.
33. In the notes of arguments and oral argument, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.2 the insurance company of the autorickshaw stated that as on the date of accident Yogesh who Thanisha Shaik Alias Thanusha vs Shivaram on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106852366/
6 drove autorickshaw had no licence to drive the passenger autorickshaw, Auto bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 , had no permit and no Fitness Certificate, therefore, respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 by relying on the following judgments:
1. 2022 Live Law (Kar) 74 , M.F.A.No.100096/2019 (MV) ( Mahantesh Vs.
Netharavati and others) D.D. 25.02.2022.
2. AIR 2020 SC 4453 ( Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and another ) D.D. 23.09.2020 3. MFA No.100226/2016 and 100730 /2016 D.D.22.04.2012) (Smt.Padma and others Vs. Ramanjali Naidy and others)
4. 2008 ACJ 1307 ( Sardari and others Vs. Sushil Kumar and others) DD.04.03.2008 5. MANU/MH/3546 2018 , F.A.Nos.1491-1541/2015 (Dhondubai Vs. Hanumatappa Bandappa Gandigude and others ) D.D. 21.09.2018 6. MANU/KA/0718/2009 M.F.A. No.1837/2008 ( New India Assurance Company Limited by its Manager Vs. Smt.Padmavathamma, W/o. K.N.Venkataraju and others) D.D. 19.11.2009 34.
Hence, the judgments cited on behalf of the respondent No.2 insurance company are directly applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
39. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 is not eligible to be indemnified by the respondent No.2 insurance company .
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, respondent No.1 owner of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 alone is liable to pay 50% of the total compensation awarded above to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,24,378/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 shall pay Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6%
p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK-4861 shall deposit Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., within 3 months from today.
The respondents No.3 and 4 being the owner and insurer of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
Respondent No.4 being the insurer of container lorry bearing MH-05-AM-1759 shall deposit Rs.1,12,189/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to her bank account directly.
The petition filed by the petitioner against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
